title: [3.13] gh-157325: Fix an OOB read in the `hz` incremental decoder on a trailing `~` (gh-157333) (#158161)
consumer: not established; the trigger is the upstream fix's own regression test
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in a 1-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: reached (the trigger began (ABR BEGIN; no marker at the access in an upstream reproducer)) and completed with no fault; the trigger ended with EXIT 0

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc's blocks as child lifetimes (patch 0014, CDERIVE/CREVOKE; tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: reached (the trigger began (ABR BEGIN; no marker at the access in an upstream reproducer)) and completed with no fault; the trigger ended with EXIT 0

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion while the block's arena stays live: pymalloc links the freed block onto its own pool free list, so the platform has no free to revoke. Once pymalloc returns an emptied arena to the system allocator (insert_to_freepool, when nf == ao->ntotalpools && ao->nextarena != NULL) the platform does have a free, and after a revocation sweep the stale access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). Both outcomes are admissible; which one occurs depends on arena occupancy and sweep timing rather than on the defect, so this arm does not separate these cases. A bounds fault (si_code=1) would falsify this.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial SILENT (spatial-20261006-105111); sublet SILENT (sublet-20261006-123446); cheribsd-revocation SILENT (cheri11)
fault_sites_why: The 2026-10-10 sweep recorded no-report for this case and it carried no fault_sites. Re-run 2026-10-19 on the pinned host ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) it reports heap-buffer-overflow, READ of size 1, '0 bytes to the right of 1-byte region', at hz_decode Modules/cjkcodecs/_codecs_cn.c:417, the region allocated by PyMem_Malloc at multibytecodec.c:1183. The report disappears under PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc, so the case is NESTED by the corpus's own test.
probe_why: upstream's test passes whether or not the defective read happens -- it only asserts that the final decode raises UnicodeDecodeError, and it does either way -- so a silent arm could not be read until the access was marked. probe-157325.py marks it and also prints _testinternalcapi.pymem_getallocatorsname(), because the question on the pools arm was whether that 1-byte PyMem_Malloc went through pymalloc at all.
note: COUNTED as a miss on all three arms, and marked ◇: the defect is live and the measured binaries contain no out-of-bounds access. The source bug is an order-of-checks error in _codecs_cn.c -- `unsigned char c2 = INBYTE2;` reads inbuf[1] before REQUIRE_INBUF(2) checks there are two bytes -- and the one-byte buffer comes from decoder.decode(b'', True), where size==0 and pendingsize==1, so multibytecodec.c:1183 does PyMem_Malloc(1). NOTHING ABOUT THE MEASUREMENT IS WRONG, and each link was checked before the binary was looked at: 1 byte is not above SMALL_REQUEST_THRESHOLD so Sublet is in the path; obmalloc.c sets PYMEM_DOMAIN_MEM to PYMALLOC_ALLOC and probe-157325.py prints allocators='pymalloc' from inside the guest on both arms; pymalloc_alloc has a single exit, return block_issue(state, bp, nbytes), so both the free-list and new-pool paths are narrowed, and to the request rather than the size class; capstone_cap_derive is exact (child.bounds.end = base + size, and the exact-bounds profile this pin uses skips the compress round-trip check), so there is no granularity floor; and INBYTE2 is (*inbuf)[1] where inbuf is literally the pointer PyMem_Malloc returned. The probe reaches AT-ACCESS and then PASSED on both arms with no fault. THE BINARY SAYS WHY. All three targets guard the second load with the length check: pools `58368c beq s2, s6` (inleft==1) guarding `583690 lbu a1, 0x1(a2)`; base `583420 beq s2, s6` guarding `583424 lbu a1, 0x1(a2)`; CheriBSD `651bc4 blt s0, s6` (s6=2) guarding `651bc8 lbu a0, 0x1(a0)`. With inleft==1 the branch is taken and the load never executes. This is not an optimisation-level choice and not an ASan artefact: all four builds are -O3 -DNDEBUG -g -Wall, and the plain x86-64 build at the same -O3 DOES perform the load, scheduling it between the compare and the branch (`2fd0 cmp $0x1,%r15` / `2fd4 movzbl 0x1(%rax),%edx` / `2fd8 je`). Same source, same -O3, different backend. The methodological consequence: live_in_pin is proven on the host ASan build, not on the target binaries, so a defect can be live by that test and absent from the artefact measured. The audit is bounded to all-silent rows, which are 04, 06 and 17, and all three are checked.
